              {"tex":"0=\\frac{x}{\\sqrt{x^2+h_1^2}}-\\frac{L-x}{\\sqrt{(L-x)^2+h_2^2}}","move":{"type":"evaluate","by":"d\\ell/dx=0"},"note":"Fermat requires a stationary length within this family of reflected paths.","ask":{"q":"What condition selects the stationary path?","options":["\\(\\ell=0\\)","\\(d\\ell/dx=0\\)","\\(h_1=h_2\\)","\\(x=0\\)"],"answer":1,"why":"Stationarity sets the first derivative to zero, not the path length itself."}},
              {"tex":"\\frac{x}{\\sqrt{x^2+h_1^2}}=\\frac{L-x}{\\sqrt{(L-x)^2+h_2^2}}","move":{"type":"rearrange"},"note":"Move one geometric ratio to the other side."},
              {"phase":"Angles","tex":"\\sin i=\\sin r","move":{"type":"substitute","label":"Use the two right triangles"},"note":"Each ratio is horizontal displacement divided by ray length.","ask":{"q":"With angles measured from the normal, what is x/AP?","options":["\\(\\cos i\\)","\\(\\tan i\\)","\\(\\cot i\\)","\\(\\sin i\\)"],"answer":3,"why":"The horizontal displacement is opposite the angle measured from the vertical normal."}},
              {"tex":"i=r","move":{"type":"apply","fn":"\\arcsin"},"note":"Both ray angles lie between zero and ninety degrees.","ask":{"q":"Why does equal sine imply equal angles in this geometry?","options":["Sine is one-to-one on 0° to 90°","Every angle has the same sine","The mirror index is zero","Both angles must be 45°"],"answer":0,"why":"The physical incidence and reflection angles occupy the range where sine is one-to-one."}}
            ]},
            {"type":"math","title":"Find the bounce point","label":"Worked example","body":"For h₁ = 3 cm, h₂ = 2 cm and L = 10 cm, similar ray triangles give x/h₁ = (L−x)/h₂.","tex":"x=\\frac{h_1L}{h_1+h_2}=\\frac{3(10)}{3+2}=6\\ {\\rm cm}"},
            {"type":"mcq","time":60,"q":"A ray makes 30° with the mirror surface. What is its angle of reflection?","options":["30°","60°","90°","15°"],"answer":1,"why":"The incident angle is 90°−30° = 60° from the normal. The reflected angle equals that incident angle."},
            {"type":"fill","time":45,"q":"The incident ray, reflected ray and normal are ____.","answer":"coplanar|in the same plane","why":"Coplanarity is the first law of reflection. Equal angles is the other law."},
            {"type":"number","time":90,"q":"For equal source and destination heights with foot separation L = 12 cm, how far is P from the source's perpendicular foot?","answer":6,"tolerance":0,"unit":"cm","why":"Equal heights give a symmetric minimum path: x = L/2 = 6 cm."},
            {"type":"mcq","time":60,"q":"Why does reflecting A to A′ simplify the shortest reflected path?","options":["It changes the refractive index","It removes the fixed endpoints","AP equals A′P for every point P on the mirror","It requires normal incidence"],"answer":2,"why":"The equal distances turn the broken reflected route into a straight-line minimization problem from A′ to B."}
          ]},
          {"id":"optics-u1-refraction","title":"Snell's law from Fermat","icon":"lens","subject":"Optics Unit 1","minutes":25,"cards":[
            {"type":"intuition","term":"refraction","title":"Spend less distance in the slower medium","meaning":"Refraction changes the direction of a transmitted ray when the optical speeds differ.","picture":"Slide the crossing point along the boundary and trade distance in one medium against distance in the other.","example":"Air-to-glass light usually takes a bent route because glass has the higher index and lower speed.","bridge":"Minimize the index-weighted distance, not the unweighted geometric distance."},
            {"type":"info","title":"What is Snell's law?","defines":["snell"],"body":"Snell's law relates the refractive indices and the angles of incident and transmitted rays. Both angles are measured from the interface normal.","tex":"n_1\\sin\\theta_1=n_2\\sin\\theta_2"},
            {"type":"info","title":"The two refraction laws","body":"The incident ray, refracted ray and normal lie in one plane. Their angles satisfy Snell's law. In a uniform isotropic medium, each straight segment has its own constant speed."},
            {"type":"info","title":"Set up the refracted route","body":"A is h₁ above the interface; B is h₂ below it. Their feet are L apart.             {"type":"math","title":"Weight each leg by its index","label":"Set-up","body":"The endpoints are fixed; only x changes. With positive indices and heights, this optical path is a convex function of x.","tex":"L_{\\rm op}(x)=n_1\\sqrt{x^2+h_1^2}+n_2\\sqrt{(L-x)^2+h_2^2}"},
            {"type":"derivation","title":"Derive the law of refraction","legend":"\\(\\theta_1,\\theta_2\\): angles from the normal; \\(n_1,n_2\\): constant indices; \\(h_1,h_2,L\\): fixed distances.","phases":[{"name":"Optical path","why":"Add the two index-weighted distances."},{"name":"Stationarity","why":"Vary the boundary crossing point."},{"name":"Snell's law","why":"Convert the length ratios into sines."}],"steps":[
              {"phase":"Optical path","tex":"L_{\\rm op}=n_1\\sqrt{x^2+h_1^2}+n_2\\sqrt{(L-x)^2+h_2^2}","note":"Use the optical path, since the two segments have different speeds."},
              {"phase":"Stationarity","tex":"\\frac{dL_{\\rm op}}{dx}=\\frac{n_1x}{\\sqrt{x^2+h_1^2}}-\\frac{n_2(L-x)}{\\sqrt{(L-x)^2+h_2^2}}","move":{"type":"differentiate","wrt":"x"},"note":"Apply the chain rule to both square roots.","ask":{"q":"Why is the second derivative contribution negative in this first-derivative expression?","options":["The second index is negative","The second height changes sign","d(L−x)/dx is −1","The light travels backwards in time"],"answer":2,"why":"Moving R to the right increases x but reduces L−x. The minus sign comes from the chain rule."}},
              {"tex":"0=\\frac{n_1x}{\\sqrt{x^2+h_1^2}}-\\frac{n_2(L-x)}{\\sqrt{(L-x)^2+h_2^2}}","move":{"type":"evaluate","by":"dL_{\\rm op}/dx=0"},"note":"Set the optical-path derivative to zero at the ray's crossing point.","ask":{"q":"What is the correct stationary condition?","options":["\\(L_{\\rm op}=0\\)","\\(dL_{\\rm op}/dx=0\\)","\\(n_1=n_2\\)","\\(x=L\\)"],"answer":1,"why":"Fermat's principle requires the first-order variation to vanish, while the path length stays positive."}},
              {"tex":"\\frac{n_1x}{\\sqrt{x^2+h_1^2}}=\\frac{n_2(L-x)}{\\sqrt{(L-x)^2+h_2^2}}","move":{"type":"rearrange"},"note":"Equate the two weighted geometric ratios."},
              {"phase":"Snell's law","tex":"n_1\\sin\\theta_1=\\frac{n_2(L-x)}{\\sqrt{(L-x)^2+h_2^2}}","move":{"type":"substitute","by":"\\sin\\theta_1=x/\\sqrt{x^2+h_1^2}"},"note":"The first ratio is the sine of incidence measured from the normal.","ask":{"q":"Which ratio equals \\(\\sin\\theta_1\\)?","options":["\\(x/\\sqrt{x^2+h_1^2}\\)","\\(h_1/\\sqrt{x^2+h_1^2}\\)","\\(x/h_1\\)","\\(h_1/x\\)"],"answer":0,"why":"The horizontal distance x is opposite θ₁ in the right triangle."}},
              {"tex":"n_1\\sin\\theta_1=n_2\\sin\\theta_2","move":{"type":"substitute","by":"\\sin\\theta_2=(L-x)/\\sqrt{(L-x)^2+h_2^2}"},"note":"Replace the second ratio to obtain Snell's law.","ask":{"q":"Which index multiplies the sine of the refracted angle?","options":["Always 1","The incident index n₁","The difference n₂−n₁","The transmitted-medium index n₂"],"answer":3,"why":"Each sine is weighted by the refractive index of its own ray segment."}}
            ]},
            {"type":"info","title":"Which way does the ray bend?","body":"For nonzero incidence into a higher-index medium, θ₂ < θ₁: the ray bends toward the normal. Into a lower-index medium it bends away, whenever a transmitted ray exists."},
            {"type":"info","title":"Normal incidence and equal indices","body":"At normal incidence, θ₁ = θ₂ = 0: there is no directional bending even if speed changes. If n₁ = n₂, the transmitted ray is undeviated at every allowed incidence angle."},
            {"type":"math","title":"Air into glass at 30°","label":"Worked example","body":"Use n₁ = 1.00, n₂ = 1.50 and θ₁ = 30°. Take the inverse sine in degrees.","tex":"\\theta_2=\\sin^{-1}\\!\\left(\\frac{1.00}{1.50}\\sin30^\\circ\\right)\\approx19.47^\\circ"},
            {"type":"mcq","time":60,"q":"A ray enters a higher-index medium at oblique incidence.             {"type":"fill","time":45,"q":"The incidence and refraction angles in Snell's law are measured from the ____.","answer":"normal|surface normal|interface normal","why":"Measuring from the surface instead would require complementary angles and cosine factors."},
            {"type":"number","time":90,"q":"With n₁ = 1, n₂ = 2 and θ₁ = 30°, what is sin θ₂?","answer":0.25,"tolerance":0.001,"unit":"","why":"sin θ₂ = (1/2) × sin 30° = (1/2) × (1/2) = 0.25."},
            {"type":"mcq","time":60,"q":"At normal incidence into glass from air, what changes?","options":["Direction changes, speed stays the same","Both direction and speed must stay the same","Speed changes, direction stays the same","The refracted angle becomes 90°"],"answer":2,"why":"Snell's law keeps both angles at zero; v = c/n decreases when the index increases."}

            {"type":"info","title":"What is reversibility?","defines":["reversibility"],"body":"In the reciprocal media used here, a ray can retrace its path when its direction reverses. Reflection and Snell's law remain satisfied with source and destination exchanged."},
            {"type":"math","title":"Find an unknown index","label":"Worked example","body":"Light comes from air with incidence 45° and refracts at 30°.             {"type":"math","title":"Reverse the air-to-glass example","label":"Worked example","body":"A glass ray (n₁ = 1.5) at 19.47° travels into air (n₂ = 1). It retraces the earlier 30° air ray, to rounding precision.","tex":"\\sin\\theta_2=1.5\\sin19.47^\\circ\\approx0.5000"},
            {"type":"info","title":"What is the critical angle?","defines":["critical-angle"],"body":"For n₁ > n₂, the critical angle gives a refracted angle of 90°.             {"type":"info","title":"What is total internal reflection?","defines":["tir"],"body":"Total internal reflection occurs from higher to lower index when incidence exceeds the critical angle. Equal-to-critical incidence is the limiting grazing case, not an angle above the threshold."},
            {"type":"math","title":"Check whether refraction is possible","label":"Application of Snell's law","body":"Glass to air at 50°, with n₁ = 1.5 and n₂ = 1. The required sine exceeds one, so there is total internal reflection.","tex":"\\frac{n_1}{n_2}\\sin50^\\circ\\approx1.149>1"},
            {"type":"math","title":"A longer route can be faster","label":"Compare trial paths","body":"Trial A has 1.0 m in air and 1.0 m in glass (n = 1.5).             {"type":"info","title":"A reliable solution sequence","body":"Draw the normal. Label each medium and its angle. Write the stationary optical path or the resulting law. Check the bending direction, units and whether a calculated sine lies between zero and one."},
            {"type":"mcq","time":60,"q":"Which condition permits total internal reflection?","options":["Lower-to-higher index at any angle","Higher-to-lower index above the critical angle","Equal indices at normal incidence","Higher-to-lower index below the critical angle"],"answer":1,"why":"Only higher-to-lower-index transmission can require sin θ₂ > 1.             {"type":"number","time":90,"q":"For n₁ = 2 and n₂ = 1, what is the critical angle in degrees?","answer":30,"tolerance":0.01,"unit":"°","why":"At the critical angle, sin θc = n₂/n₁ = 1/2, so θc = 30°."},
            {"type":"mcq","time":60,"q":"A Snell calculation gives sin θ₂ = 1.2.             {"type":"fill","time":45,"q":"The ability of a ray to retrace its optical route is called ____.","answer":"reversibility|ray reversibility|reversibility of light","why":"Swapping source and destination preserves the reflection and refraction laws in these reciprocal media."}

            {"type":"info","title":"What is a parabola?","defines":["parabola"],"body":"A parabola consists of points equally distant from a fixed focus and a fixed directrix. Rotating it around its axis makes a paraboloidal reflector."},

        feedback(c.el, (timedOut ? '<b>Time’s up.</b> Answer: ' + correctText(c) + '. ' : ok ? '<b>Correct.</b> ' : '<b>Not quite.</b> Answer: ' + correctText(c) + '. ') + (c.why || ''));

    # Optics Unit 1
    
    Fermat's principle and the laws of reflection and refraction, using the
    Study Day 9 interface.
    
    **Hosted app:** http://100.97.67.103:8792/
    
    Open the URL from a device connected to the same Tailscale network.
    Hosting runs on `optima-3` while the computer and service are running.
    
    ## Study
    
    - Six topics, 76 authored cards, 30 glossary definitions.
    - Four guided derivations with 16 decision checkpoints; 24 scored quizzes.
    - Plane-mirror, refraction, parabolic and elliptical ray diagrams.
    - Click a section pile, then a topic cover; swipe or use arrow keys to browse.
    - Tap dotted terms for definitions. Flip definition cards for eight-word recall,
      reveal the reference statement, then confirm or retry.
    - Match mode retains independent topic unlocking, configurable halves and
      breaks, pause/resume and locally saved progress.
    - Use the football button for Match centre, `=` for the calculator, and the
      **PDF** link beside the notch for the copied six-page source.
    - Study allocations total 120 minutes; breaks are additional.
    
    Progress is stored in this browser under a separate course key. MathJax and fonts
    use external CDNs on first load. The direct HTTP Tailscale address supports the
    study app, but browser installation/service-worker offline support requires
    HTTPS (or a localhost preview).
    
    ## Files and rebuild
    
    - `unit-1-fermat-laws-reflection-refraction.pdf`: original Sem 5 extract.
    - `index.html`: standalone page.
    - `app/`: hosted page, PDF, icons and manifest.
    - `study-match/data/data.json`: directly authored educational content.
    - `study-match/src/`: copied UI with Unit 1 header, PDF link and scoped cache.

    ```

    reads those files directly, so rebuilding updates the hosted app.

    systemctl --user status optics-unit-1
    ```
    
    Start it again after a reboot with:
    
    ```sh
    systemd-run --user --unit=optics-unit-1 \
      --description='Optics Unit 1 study app' --property=Restart=on-failure \
      /usr/bin/python3 -m http.server 8792 --bind 100.97.67.103 \
      --directory /home/ihjas/Documents/GitHub/SSC-FILES/SSC-V6/optics-unit-1/app
    ```

    # Optics Unit 1 — source and scope
    
    Primary source: Ajoy Ghatak, *Optics*, 6th edition, chapter 3, §§3.1–3.2.
    The supplied six-page extract is copied byte-for-byte from:
    
    `STUDY-PLAN-V5/sources/sem5/phy/optics/module-1/unit-1-fermat-laws-reflection-refraction.pdf`
    
    The Semester 5 unit map assigns Unit 1 to **laws of reflection and refraction
    from Fermat's principle** (full-book PDF pages 56–61). The copy at the project
    root and the hosted copy retain the entire extract.
    
    ## Coverage
    
    - Rays and the short-wavelength approximation; refractive index; optical versus
      geometric path; travel time as optical path divided by c.
    - The stationary form of Fermat's principle, fixed endpoints, nearby allowed
      routes, straight rays in a uniform isotropic medium, and the limits of “least
      time” wording.
    - Reflection: the image construction, coplanarity, and a detailed calculus
      derivation of equal angles.
    - Refraction: the two-medium geometry, chain-rule sign, coplanarity, and a
      detailed derivation of Snell's law.
    - Original numerical examples, angle conventions, reversibility, and
      critical-angle/total-internal-reflection checks as applications of Snell's law.
    - The source's parabolic and elliptical reflector examples, with an explicit
      equal-path derivation for a parabola and an introduction to virtual images.
    
    The extract includes Example 3.3 on spherical refraction and the beginning of
    §3.3 on inhomogeneous media. Those pages remain in the PDF; detailed spherical
    imaging is the next mapped unit and is not presented as a required Unit 1 topic.
    
    ## Source correction
    
    Printed page 3.6, Eq. (3.6), has **n₁ sin θ₁ = n₁ sin θ₂**. The second index is
    a typographical error. Eq. (3.5), Fig. 3.5 and the preceding weighted-path
    derivation give **n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂**, which the app uses. The PDF is unchanged.
    
    All explanations, glossary entries, diagrams, examples, questions and
    derivation checkpoints were authored directly in `study-match/data/data.json`.
    The calculations and source diagrams informed the content; the PDF's text was
    not automatically transformed into cards.
    
    ## Interface provenance
    
    The builder and UI source were copied from `study-day-9/study-match`.
    The original Day 9 project is unchanged. The new course title gives this deck
    its own local-storage key. Its service-worker cache has a unit-specific prefix.

          page.on('pageerror', e => errors.push(e.message));
          const response = await page.goto(url, {waitUntil:'networkidle'});
          assert.equal(response.status(), 200);
          await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__sm && typeof MathJax.tex2svg === 'function');
        }
        async function show(page, sheetId, type, title) {
          const id = await page.evaluate(({sheetId,type,title}) => {
            const sh = __sm.SHEETS.find(s => s.id === sheetId);
            const c = sh.cards.find(c => c.type === type && (!title || c.title === title));
            if (!c) throw Error('Missing requested card: ' + type + ' / ' + title);
            sh.el.closest('.group').classList.remove('is-stacked');
            if (!sh.el.classList.contains('is-open')) sh.el.querySelector('.cover').click();
            __sm.glideTo(c.el, 700);
            return c.id;
          }, {sheetId,type,title});
          await page.waitForFunction(id => __sm.centred()?.dataset.card === id, id);
          await page.waitForTimeout(400);
          return page.locator('[data-card="' + id + '"]');

    # 03 — SVG pictures for `info` cards
    
    Pictures are simple, flat diagrams. The app colours them, including in dark mode, through
    **classes**. Never write colours yourself.
    
    ## Hard rules
    
    - Exactly one element: `<svg viewBox="0 0 260 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="what it shows">…</svg>`
    - Draw inside x 0–260, y 0–180. Leave ~8 units of margin.
    - Allowed elements: `circle, ellipse, rect, line, polyline, polygon, path, text, g`.
    - **No** `fill="#…"`, `stroke="#…"`, `style=`, `<script>`, `<image>`, `href`, `on…=` attributes, gradients, filters, fonts.
    - Use only these classes:
    
    | class | effect | use for |
    |---|---|---|
    | `f` | solid main colour (violet) | main objects, nuclei, arrows heads |
    | `s` | soft fill (pale lavender) | backgrounds, secondary objects, areas |
    | `ok` | violet outline (add to a filled shape: `class="s ok"`) | borders |
    | `lk` | violet line, no fill | lines, paths, axes, orbits |
    | `gk` | faint grey line | ground lines, guides, dashed helpers |
    | `h` | amber fill | the ONE thing to look at (electron, ball, key point) |
    | `hk` | amber line, no fill | the ONE key arrow or path |
    | `t` | text in ink colour, bold | labels on light backgrounds |
    | `i` | text in light colour, bold | labels on top of `f` shapes |
    
    - Set line thickness with `stroke-width="2"` (allowed). Dashes with `stroke-dasharray="5 5"` (allowed).
    - Text: `font-size` 11–26, `text-anchor="middle"` to centre. Max ~4 words per label.
    - Only **one** amber (`h`/`hk`) highlight per picture: it is where the eye goes.
    - Inside the JSON string, every `"` in the SVG must be written `\"`.
    
    ## Example (as it appears inside data.json)
    
    ```json
    "art": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 260 180\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" role=\"img\" aria-label=\"Sodium ion giving an electron to a chloride ion\"><circle cx=\"80\" cy=\"95\" r=\"50\" class=\"s\"/><text x=\"80\" y=\"104\" text-anchor=\"middle\" font-size=\"24\" class=\"t\">Na⁺</text><circle cx=\"180\" cy=\"95\" r=\"50\" class=\"f\"/><text x=\"180\" y=\"104\" text-anchor=\"middle\" font-size=\"24\" class=\"i\">Cl⁻</text><path d=\"M 112 62 Q 130 22 148 62\" class=\"hk\" stroke-width=\"2.5\" stroke-dasharray=\"5 5\"/><circle cx=\"130\" cy=\"32\" r=\"6\" class=\"h\"/></svg>"
    ```
    
    ## Good subjects for a picture
    
    Particles and charges, forces as arrows, rays and lenses, simple graphs (axes + one line + shaded
    area), before/after comparisons side by side, cycles as circles with arrows, cells as ellipses.
    
    If a picture would need more than ~15 shapes, skip `art` and use `"tex"` for a key formula instead.
    
    ## Physics subjects: required pictures (added 2026-10-23)

    name: "imagegen"
    description: "Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas."
    ---
    
    # Image Generation Skill
    
    Generates or edits images for the current project (for example website assets, game assets, UI mockups, product mockups, wireframes, logo design, photorealistic images, or infographics).
    
    ## Top-level modes and rules
    
    This skill has exactly two top-level modes:
    
    - **Default built-in tool mode (preferred):** built-in `image_gen` tool for image generation, editing, and transparent-image requests. Does not require `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
    - **Fallback CLI mode:** `scripts/image_gen.py` CLI. Use when the user explicitly asks for or confirms the CLI/API/model path. Requires `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
    
    Within CLI fallback, the CLI exposes three subcommands:
    
    - `generate`
    - `edit`
    - `generate-batch`
    
    Rules:
    - Use the built-in `image_gen` tool by default for normal image generation and editing requests.
    - Do not switch to CLI fallback for ordinary quality, size, or file-path control.
    - For transparent images, ask built-in `image_gen` for a transparent background and preserve the generated alpha.
    - Never silently switch from built-in `image_gen` or CLI `gpt-image-2` to CLI `gpt-image-1.5`; ask the user first unless they explicitly requested `gpt-image-1.5`.
    - The word `batch` by itself does not mean CLI fallback. If the user asks for many assets or says to batch-generate assets without explicitly asking for CLI/API/model controls, stay on the built-in path and issue one built-in call per requested asset or variant.
    - If the built-in tool fails or is unavailable, tell the user the CLI fallback exists and that it requires `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Proceed only if the user explicitly asks for that fallback.
    - If the user explicitly asks for CLI mode, use the bundled `scripts/image_gen.py` workflow. Do not create one-off SDK runners.
    - Never modify `scripts/image_gen.py`. If something is missing, ask the user before doing anything else.
    
    Built-in save-path policy:
    - In built-in tool mode, Codex saves generated images under `$CODEX_HOME/*` by default.
    - Do not describe or rely on OS temp as the default built-in destination.
    - Do not describe or rely on a destination-path argument (if any) on the built-in `image_gen` tool. If a specific location is needed, generate first and then move or copy the selected output from `$CODEX_HOME/generated_images/...`.
    - Save-path precedence in built-in mode:
      1. If the user names a destination, move or copy the selected output there.
      2. If the image is meant for the current project, move or copy the final selected image into the workspace before finishing.
      3. If the image is only for preview or brainstorming, render it inline; the underlying file can remain at the default `$CODEX_HOME/*` path.
    - Never leave a project-referenced asset only at the default `$CODEX_HOME/*` path.
    - Do not overwrite an existing asset unless the user explicitly asked for replacement; otherwise create a sibling versioned filename such as `hero-v2.png` or `item-icon-edited.png`.
    
    Shared prompt guidance for both modes lives in `references/prompting.md` and `references/sample-prompts.md`.
    
    Fallback-only docs/resources for CLI mode:
    - `references/cli.md`
    - `references/image-api.md`
    - `references/codex-network.md`
    - `scripts/image_gen.py`
    
    ## When to use
    - Generate a new image (concept art, product shot, cover, website hero)
    - Generate a new image using one or more reference images for style, composition, or mood
    - Edit an existing image (inpainting, lighting or weather transformations, background replacement, object removal, compositing, transparent background)
    - Produce many assets or variants for one task
    
    ## When not to use
    - Extending or matching an existing SVG/vector icon set, logo system, or illustration library inside the repo
    - Creating simple shapes, diagrams, wireframes, or icons that are better produced directly in SVG, HTML/CSS, or canvas
    - Making a small project-local asset edit when the source file already exists in an editable native format
    - Any task where the user clearly wants deterministic code-native output instead of a generated bitmap
    
    ## Decision tree
    
    Think about two separate questions:
    
    1. **Intent:** is this a new image or an edit of an existing image?
    2. **Execution strategy:** is this one asset or many assets/variants?
    
    Intent:
    - If the user wants to modify an existing image while preserving parts of it, treat the request as **edit**.
    - If the user provides images only as references for style, composition, mood, or subject guidance, treat the request as **generate**.
    - If the user provides no images, treat the request as **generate**.
    
    Built-in edit semantics:
    - Built-in edit mode is for images already visible in the conversation context, such as attached images or images generated earlier in the thread.
    - If the user wants to edit a local image file with the built-in tool, first load it with built-in `view_image` tool so the image is visible in the conversation context, then proceed with the built-in edit flow.
    - Do not promise arbitrary filesystem-path editing through the built-in tool.
    - If a local file still needs direct file-path control, masks, or other explicit CLI-only parameters, use the explicit CLI fallback only when the user asks for it.
    - For edits, preserve invariants aggressively and save non-destructively by default.
    
    Execution strategy:
    - In the built-in default path, produce many assets or variants by issuing one `image_gen` call per requested asset or variant.
    - In the CLI fallback path, use the CLI `generate-batch` subcommand only when the user explicitly chose CLI mode and needs many prompts/assets.
    - For many distinct assets, do not use `n` as a substitute for separate prompts. `n` is for variants of one prompt; distinct assets need distinct built-in calls or distinct CLI `generate-batch` jobs.
    
    Assume the user wants a new image unless they clearly ask to change an existing one.
    
    ## Workflow
    1. Decide the top-level mode: built-in by default, including transparent-output requests; fallback CLI only if explicitly requested or confirmed.
    2. Decide the intent: `generate` or `edit`.
    3. Decide whether the output is preview-only or meant to be consumed by the current project.
    4. Decide the execution strategy: single asset vs repeated built-in calls vs CLI `generate-batch`.
    5. Collect inputs up front: prompt(s), exact text (verbatim), constraints/avoid list, and any input images.
    6. For every input image, label its role explicitly:
       - reference image
       - edit target
       - supporting insert/style/compositing input
    7. If the edit target is only on the local filesystem and you are staying on the built-in path, inspect it with `view_image` first so the image is available in conversation context.
    8. If the user asked for a photo, illustration, sprite, product image, banner, or other explicitly raster-style asset, use `image_gen` rather than substituting SVG/HTML/CSS placeholders. If the request is for an icon, logo, or UI graphic that should match existing repo-native SVG/vector/code assets, prefer editing those directly instead.
    9. Augment the prompt based on specificity:
       - If the user's prompt is already specific and detailed, normalize it into a clear spec without adding creative requirements.
       - If the user's prompt is generic, add tasteful augmentation only when it materially improves output quality.
    10. Use the built-in `image_gen` tool by default.
    11. For transparent-output requests, ask built-in `image_gen` for a transparent background and preserve the generated alpha channel.
    12. Inspect outputs and validate: subject, style, composition, text accuracy, and invariants/avoid items.
    13. Iterate with a single targeted change, then re-check.
    14. For preview-only work, render the image inline; the underlying file may remain at the default `$CODEX_HOME/generated_images/...` path.
    15. For project-bound work, move or copy the selected artifact into the workspace and update any consuming code or references. Never leave a project-referenced asset only at the default `$CODEX_HOME/generated_images/...` path.
    16. For batches or multi-asset requests, persist every requested deliverable final in the workspace unless the user explicitly asked to keep outputs preview-only. Discarded variants do not need to be kept unless requested.
    17. If the user explicitly chooses or confirms the CLI fallback, then use the fallback-only docs for model, quality, size, `input_fidelity`, masks, output format, output paths, and network setup.
    18. Always report the final saved path(s) for any workspace-bound asset(s), plus the final prompt or prompt set and whether the built-in tool or fallback CLI mode was used.
    
    ## Transparent image requests
    
    Ask built-in `image_gen` for a genuinely transparent background and preserve its alpha.
    
    ## Prompt augmentation
    
    Reformat user prompts into a structured, production-oriented spec. Make the user's goal clearer and more actionable, but do not blindly add detail.
    
    Treat this as prompt-shaping guidance, not a closed schema. Use only the lines that help, and add a short extra labeled line when it materially improves clarity.
    
    ### Specificity policy
    
    Use the user's prompt specificity to decide how much augmentation is appropriate:
    
    - If the prompt is already specific and detailed, preserve that specificity and only normalize/structure it.
    - If the prompt is generic, you may add tasteful augmentation when it will materially improve the result.
    
    Allowed augmentations:
    - composition or framing hints
    - polish level or intended-use hints
    - practical layout guidance
    - reasonable scene concreteness that supports the stated request
    
    Not allowed augmentations:
    - extra characters or objects that are not implied by the request
    - brand names, slogans, palettes, or narrative beats that are not implied
    - arbitrary side-specific placement unless the surrounding layout supports it
    
    ## Use-case taxonomy (exact slugs)
    
    Classify each request into one of these buckets and keep the slug consistent across prompts and references.
    
    Generate:
    - photorealistic-natural — candid/editorial lifestyle scenes with real texture and natural lighting.
    - product-mockup — product/packaging shots, catalog imagery, merch concepts.
    - ui-mockup — app/web interface mockups and wireframes; specify the desired fidelity.
    - infographic-diagram — diagrams/infographics with structured layout and text.
    - scientific-educational — classroom explainers, scientific diagrams, and learning visuals with required labels and accuracy constraints.
    - ads-marketing — campaign concepts and ad creatives with audience, brand position, scene, and exact tagline/copy.
    - productivity-visual — slide, chart, workflow, and data-heavy business visuals.
    - logo-brand — logo/mark exploration, vector-friendly.
    - illustration-story — comics, children’s book art, narrative scenes.
    - stylized-concept — style-driven concept art, 3D/stylized renders.
    - historical-scene — period-accurate/world-knowledge scenes.
    
    Edit:
    - text-localization — translate/replace in-image text, preserve layout.
    - identity-preserve — try-on, person-in-scene; lock face/body/pose.
    - precise-object-edit — remove/replace a specific element (including interior swaps).
    - lighting-weather — time-of-day/season/atmosphere changes only.
    - background-extraction — transparent background / clean cutout. Ask built-in `image_gen` for actual transparency.
    - style-transfer — apply reference style while changing subject/scene.
    - compositing — multi-image insert/merge with matched lighting/perspective.
    - sketch-to-render — drawing/line art to photoreal render.
    
    ## Shared prompt schema
    
    Use the following labeled spec as shared prompt scaffolding for both top-level modes:
    
    ```text
    Use case: <taxonomy slug>
    Asset type: <where the asset will be used>
    Primary request: <user's main prompt>
    Input images: <Image 1: role; Image 2: role> (optional)
    Scene/backdrop: <environment>
    Subject: <main subject>
    Style/medium: <photo/illustration/3D/etc>
    Composition/framing: <wide/close/top-down; placement>
    Lighting/mood: <lighting + mood>
    Color palette: <palette notes>
    Materials/textures: <surface details>
    Text (verbatim): "<exact text>"
    Constraints: <must keep/must avoid>
    Avoid: <negative constraints>
    ```
    
    Notes:
    - `Asset type` and `Input images` are prompt scaffolding, not dedicated CLI flags.
    - `Scene/backdrop` refers to the visual setting. It is not the same as the fallback CLI `background` parameter, which controls output transparency behavior.
    - Fallback-only execution notes such as `Quality:`, `Input fidelity:`, masks, output format, and output paths belong in the CLI path only. Do not treat them as built-in `image_gen` tool arguments.
    
    Augmentation rules:
    - Keep it short.
    - Add only the details needed to improve the prompt materially.
    - For edits, explicitly list invariants (`change only X; keep Y unchanged`).
    - If any critical detail is missing and blocks success, ask a question; otherwise proceed.
    
    ## Examples
    
    ### Generation example (hero image)
    ```text
    Use case: product-mockup
    Asset type: landing page hero
    Primary request: a minimal hero image of a ceramic coffee mug
    Style/medium: clean product photography
    Composition/framing: wide composition with usable negative space for page copy if needed
    Lighting/mood: soft studio lighting
    Constraints: no logos, no text, no watermark
    ```
    
    ### Edit example (invariants)
    ```text
    Use case: precise-object-edit
    Asset type: product photo background replacement
    Primary request: replace only the background with a warm sunset gradient
    Constraints: change only the background; keep the product and its edges unchanged; no text; no watermark
    ```
    
    ## Prompting best practices
    - Structure prompt as scene/backdrop -> subject -> details -> constraints.
    - Include intended use (ad, UI mock, infographic) to set the mode and polish level.
    - Use camera/composition language for photorealism.
    - Only use SVG/vector stand-ins when the user explicitly asked for vector output or a non-image placeholder.
    - Quote exact text and specify typography + placement.
    - For tricky words, spell them letter-by-letter and require verbatim rendering.
    - For multi-image inputs, reference images by index and describe how they should be used.
    - For edits, repeat invariants every iteration to reduce drift.
    - Iterate with single-change follow-ups.
    - If the prompt is generic, add only the extra detail that will materially help.
    - If the prompt is already detailed, normalize it instead of expanding it.
    - For CLI fallback only, see `references/cli.md` and `references/image-api.md` for model, `quality`, `input_fidelity`, masks, output format, and output-path guidance.
    - For transparent images, ask built-in `image_gen` for actual transparency and preserve its alpha.
    
    More principles shared by both modes: `references/prompting.md`.
    Copy/paste specs shared by both modes: `references/sample-prompts.md`.
    
    ## Guidance by asset type
    Asset-type templates (website assets, game assets, wireframes, logo) are consolidated in `references/sample-prompts.md`.
    
    ## gpt-image-2 guidance for CLI fallback
    
    The fallback CLI defaults to `gpt-image-2`.
    
    - Use `gpt-image-2` for new CLI/API workflows unless the user confirms a different model.
    - CLI `gpt-image-2` does not support `background=transparent`; ask before using `gpt-image-1.5` unless the user explicitly requested that model.
    - `gpt-image-2` always uses high fidelity for image inputs; do not set `input_fidelity` with this model.
    - `gpt-image-2` supports `quality` values `low`, `medium`, `high`, and `auto`.
    - Use `quality low` for fast drafts, thumbnails, and quick iterations. Use `medium`, `high`, or `auto` for final assets, dense text, diagrams, identity-sensitive edits, or high-resolution outputs.
    - Square images are typically fastest to generate. Use `1024x1024` for fast square drafts.
    - If the user asks for 4K-style output, use `3840x2160` for landscape or `2160x3840` for portrait.
    - `gpt-image-2` size may be `auto` or `WIDTHxHEIGHT` if all constraints hold: max edge `<= 3840px`, both edges multiples of `16px`, long-to-short ratio `<= 3:1`, total pixels between `655,360` and `8,294,400`.
    
    Popular `gpt-image-2` sizes:
    - `1024x1024` square
    - `1536x1024` landscape
    - `1024x1536` portrait
    - `2048x2048` 2K square
    - `2048x1152` 2K landscape
    - `3840x2160` 4K landscape
    - `2160x3840` 4K portrait
    - `auto`
    
    ## Fallback CLI mode only
    
    ### Temp and output conventions
    These conventions apply only to the CLI fallback. They do not describe built-in `image_gen` output behavior.
    - Use `tmp/imagegen/` for intermediate files (for example JSONL batches); delete them when done.
    - Write final artifacts under `output/imagegen/`.
    - Use `--out` or `--out-dir` to control output paths; keep filenames stable and descriptive.
    
    ### Dependencies
    Prefer `uv` for dependency management in this repo.
    
    Required Python package:
    ```bash
    uv pip install openai
    ```
    
    Optional for image inspection and downscaling:
    ```bash
    uv pip install pillow
    ```
    
    Portability note:
    - If you are using the installed skill outside this repo, install dependencies into that environment with its package manager.
    - In uv-managed environments, `uv pip install ...` remains the preferred path.
    
    ### Environment
    - `OPENAI_API_KEY` must be set for live API calls.
    - Do not ask the user for `OPENAI_API_KEY` when using the built-in `image_gen` tool.
    - Never ask the user to paste the full key in chat. Ask them to set it locally and confirm when ready.
    
    If the key is missing, give the user these steps:
    1. Create an API key in the OpenAI platform UI: https://platform.openai.com/api-keys
    2. Set `OPENAI_API_KEY` as an environment variable in their system.
    3. Offer to guide them through setting the environment variable for their OS/shell if needed.
    
    If installation is not possible in this environment, tell the user which dependency is missing and how to install it into their active environment.
    
    ### Script-mode notes
    - CLI commands + examples: `references/cli.md`
    - API parameter quick reference: `references/image-api.md`
    - Network approvals / sandbox settings for CLI mode: `references/codex-network.md`
    
    ## Reference map
    - `references/prompting.md`: shared prompting principles for both modes.
    - `references/sample-prompts.md`: shared copy/paste prompt recipes for both modes.
    - `references/cli.md`: fallback-only CLI usage via `scripts/image_gen.py`.
    - `references/image-api.md`: fallback-only API/CLI parameter reference.
    - `references/codex-network.md`: fallback-only network/sandbox troubleshooting for CLI mode.
    - `scripts/image_gen.py`: fallback-only CLI implementation. Use only when the user explicitly chooses or confirms CLI mode.

    .card.mf-card { padding: 14px 12px; gap: 9px; }
    .mf-top { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; }
    .mf-count { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--muted); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
    .mf-phases { display: flex; gap: 5px; overflow-x: auto; scrollbar-width: none; }
    .mf-phases::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }
    .mf-ph { flex: 0 0 auto; font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 700; padding: 4px 8px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--lav); color: var(--muted); transition: background 0.3s, color 0.3s; }
    .mf-ph.is-past { color: var(--sage); }
    .mf-ph.is-now { background: var(--violet); color: var(--on-violet); }
    .mf-board {
      flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 110px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center;
      border-radius: 16px; background-color: var(--lav);
      background-image: linear-gradient(var(--grid) 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(90deg, var(--grid) 1px, transparent 1px);
      background-size: 16px 16px; padding: 8px 0; position: relative; overflow: hidden;
    }
    .mf-stage { position: relative; width: 100%; pointer-events: none; user-select: none; }
    .mf-sp { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; overflow: visible; color: var(--ink); transform-origin: 2px 2px; transition: color 0.6s ease; will-change: transform, opacity; }
    .mf-sp path, .mf-sp rect { fill: currentColor; stroke: none; }
    .mf-sp.is-new, .mf-sp.is-op { color: var(--hl); }
    .mf-sp.is-out { color: var(--coral); }
    .mf-ghost { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; color: var(--ink-2); transform-origin: 0 0; white-space: nowrap;
      transition: transform 0.75s cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1), opacity 0.75s ease; }
    .mf-ghost svg { display: block; }
    .mf-strike { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; height: 2.5px; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--coral); transform-origin: 0 50%; }
    .mf-box { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; overflow: visible; }
    .mf-box rect { fill: none; stroke: var(--amber); stroke-width: 2.2; }
    .mf-err { position: absolute; left: 6px; right: 6px; font: 600 11px/1.4 ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; color: var(--coral); background: var(--coral-bg); border-radius: 8px; padding: 6px 8px; white-space: pre-wrap; word-break: break-all; }
    .mf-note { font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.45; font-weight: 600; color: var(--ink-2); min-height: 38px; transition: opacity 0.2s ease; }
    .mf-note b { color: var(--ink); }
    .mf-dots { display: flex; gap: 4px; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; }
    .mf-dot { appearance: none; border: 0; cursor: pointer; height: 7px; width: 7px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--lav-2); padding: 0; transition: width 0.3s ease, background 0.3s; }
    .mf-dot.is-ask { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--amber-bg), 0 0 0 3px var(--amber); }
    .mf-dot.is-done { background: var(--violet); opacity: 0.45; }
    .mf-dot.is-now { width: 18px; background: var(--violet); opacity: 1; }
    .mf-ctrl { display: flex; gap: 6px; align-items: center; }
    .mf-ctrl .chip { min-width: 38px; text-align: center; padding: 7px 8px; }
    .mf-ctrl .mf-play { background: var(--violet); color: var(--on-violet); }
    .mf-panel, .mf-ask { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; }

    .mf-ask-tag { align-self: flex-start; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.07em; text-transform: uppercase; background: var(--amber-bg); color: var(--hl); border-radius: 999px; padding: 4px 9px; }
    .mf-ask-q { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.35; }
    .mf-ask-opts { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 6px; }
    .mf-ask-opts button { appearance: none; border: 0; cursor: pointer; background: var(--lav); color: var(--ink); border-radius: 11px; padding: 8px 9px; font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 600; text-align: left; line-height: 1.3; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
    .mf-ask-opts button.is-correct { background: var(--sage-bg); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--sage); }

    # Prompting best practices
    
    These prompting principles are shared by both top-level modes of the skill:
    - built-in `image_gen` tool (default)
    - explicit `scripts/image_gen.py` CLI fallback
    
    This file is about prompt structure, specificity, and iteration. Fallback-only execution controls such as `quality`, `input_fidelity`, masks, output format, and output paths live in the fallback docs.
    
    ## Contents
    - [Structure](#structure)
    - [Specificity policy](#specificity-policy)
    - [Allowed and disallowed augmentation](#allowed-and-disallowed-augmentation)
    - [Composition and layout](#composition-and-layout)
    - [Constraints and invariants](#constraints-and-invariants)
    - [Text in images](#text-in-images)
    - [Input images and references](#input-images-and-references)
    - [Iterate deliberately](#iterate-deliberately)
    - [Transparent images](#transparent-images)
    - [Fallback-only execution controls](#fallback-only-execution-controls)
    - [Use-case tips](#use-case-tips)
    - [Where to find copy/paste recipes](#where-to-find-copypaste-recipes)
    
    ## Structure
    - Use a consistent order: scene/backdrop -> subject -> key details -> constraints -> output intent.
    - Include intended use (ad, UI mock, infographic) to set the level of polish.
    - For complex requests, use short labeled lines instead of one long paragraph.
    
    ## Specificity policy
    - If the user prompt is already specific and detailed, normalize it into a clean spec without adding creative requirements.
    - If the prompt is generic, you may add tasteful detail when it materially improves the output.
    - Treat examples in `sample-prompts.md` as fully-authored recipes, not as the default amount of augmentation to add to every request.
    - For photorealism, include `photorealistic` directly when that is the goal, plus concrete real-world texture such as pores, wrinkles, fabric wear, material grain, or imperfect everyday detail.
    
    ## Allowed and disallowed augmentation
    
    Allowed augmentation for generic prompts:
    - composition and framing cues
    - intended-use or polish-level hints
    - practical layout guidance
    - reasonable scene concreteness that supports the request
    
    Do not add:
    - extra characters, props, or objects that are not implied
    - brand palettes, slogans, or story beats that are not implied
    - arbitrary side-specific placement unless the surrounding layout supports it
    
    ## Composition and layout
    - Specify framing and viewpoint (close-up, wide, top-down) and placement only when it materially helps.
    - Call out negative space if the asset clearly needs room for UI or copy.
    - Avoid making left/right layout decisions unless the user or surrounding layout supports them.
    - For people, describe body framing, scale, gaze, and object interactions when they matter (`full body visible`, `looking down at the book`, `hands naturally gripping the handlebars`).
    
    ## Constraints and invariants
    - State what must not change (`keep background unchanged`).
    - For edits, say `change only X; keep Y unchanged` and repeat invariants on every iteration to reduce drift.
    
    ## Text in images
    - Put literal text in quotes or ALL CAPS and specify typography (font style, size, color, placement).
    - Spell uncommon words letter-by-letter if accuracy matters.
    - For in-image copy, require verbatim rendering and no extra characters.
    - In CLI fallback mode, use `medium` or `high` quality for small text, dense infographics, data-heavy slides, multi-font layouts, legends, axes, and footnotes.
    
    ## Input images and references
    - Do not assume that every provided image is an edit target.
    - Label each image by index and role (`Image 1: edit target`, `Image 2: style reference`).
    - If the user provides images for style, composition, or mood guidance and does not ask to modify them, treat the request as generation with references.
    - If the user asks to preserve an existing image while changing specific parts, treat the request as an edit.
    - For compositing, describe how the images interact (`place the subject from Image 2 into Image 1`).
    
    ## Iterate deliberately
    - Start with a clean base prompt, then make small single-change edits.
    - Re-specify critical constraints when you iterate.
    - Prefer one targeted follow-up at a time over rewriting the whole prompt.
    
    ## Transparent images
    - Ask built-in `image_gen` for a genuinely transparent background and preserve its alpha.
    
    ## Fallback-only execution controls
    - `quality`, `input_fidelity`, explicit masks, output format, and output paths are fallback-only execution controls.
    - Do not assume they are built-in `image_gen` tool arguments.

    (function () {
      var SM = window.SM;
    
      SM.initShelf = function () {
        var shelf = SM.$('shelf'), glideId = null, recallAnchor = null;
    
        function centreOffset(el) {
          var r = el.getBoundingClientRect(), sr = shelf.getBoundingClientRect();
          return shelf.scrollLeft + r.left + r.width / 2 - sr.left - shelf.clientWidth / 2;
        }
        function unfinishedAnchor() {
          if (!SM.definitionMatch() || !recallAnchor || SM.isDone(recallAnchor) ||
              !recallAnchor.sheet.el.classList.contains('is-open')) recallAnchor = null;
          return recallAnchor;
        }
        function scrollBounds() {
          var max = Infinity, boundary = null;
          if (SM.definitionMatch()) SM.SHEETS.forEach(function (sh) {
            if (!sh.el.classList.contains('is-open') || sh.el.closest('.group').classList.contains('is-stacked')) return;
            var locked = sh.cards.find(SM.cardLocked);
            if (locked && centreOffset(locked.el) < max) { boundary = locked.el; max = centreOffset(locked.el); }
          });
          var anchor = unfinishedAnchor();
          return { min: anchor ? Math.min(centreOffset(anchor.el), max) : 0, max: max, boundary: boundary };
        }
        SM.shelfBounds = scrollBounds;
        function keepDefinition(el) {
          if (glideId || !el) return;
          var r = el.getBoundingClientRect(), sr = shelf.getBoundingClientRect();
          if (Math.abs(r.left + r.width / 2 - sr.left - shelf.clientWidth / 2) > 40) return;
          if (unfinishedAnchor() && recallAnchor !== el._c) return;
          if (el && el._c && SM.definitionMatch() && SM.isDefinition(el._c) &&
              !SM.cardLocked(el._c) && !SM.isDone(el._c)) recallAnchor = el._c;
        }
        function mayLeaveDefinition() {
          if (!unfinishedAnchor()) return true;
          SM.toast('', 'Unlock this definition first', 'Confirm your answer or choose “I know this”.');
          return false;
        }
    
        function glideTo(el, duration) {
          var bounds = scrollBounds(), wanted = centreOffset(el);
          if (wanted < bounds.min - 1 && unfinishedAnchor()) el = recallAnchor.el;
          else if (wanted > bounds.max + 1 && bounds.boundary) el = bounds.boundary;
          duration = duration || 620;
          var start = performance.now();
          var fromX = el.getBoundingClientRect().left - shelf.getBoundingClientRect().left;
          var toX = shelf.clientWidth / 2 - el.getBoundingClientRect().width / 2;
          if (glideId) cancelAnimationFrame(glideId);
          shelf.style.scrollSnapType = 'none';
          function frame(now) {
            var t = Math.min((now - start) / duration, 1), eased = 1 - Math.pow(1 - t, 3);
            var wantX = fromX + (toX - fromX) * eased;
            var nowX = el.getBoundingClientRect().left - shelf.getBoundingClientRect().left;
            shelf.scrollLeft += nowX - wantX;
            if (t < 1) glideId = requestAnimationFrame(frame);
            else {
              glideId = null;
              shelf.style.scrollSnapType = '';
              var finalX = el.getBoundingClientRect().left - shelf.getBoundingClientRect().left;
              shelf.scrollTo({ left: shelf.scrollLeft + (finalX - toX), behavior: 'smooth' });
              noteCurrentReading();
            }
          }
          glideId = requestAnimationFrame(frame);
        }
        SM.glideTo = glideTo;
    
        SM.stackAll = function () {
          if (!mayLeaveDefinition()) return;
          if (glideId) { cancelAnimationFrame(glideId); glideId = null; }
          shelf.style.scrollSnapType = '';
          SM.sheetEls.forEach(function (s) { s.classList.remove('is-open'); s.querySelector('.cover').setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false'); });
          SM.groups.forEach(function (g) { g.classList.add('is-stacked'); });
          shelf.scrollTo({ left: 0, behavior: 'smooth' });
        };
